facts.fact: The National Identification Authority says its database was linked on 10 January 2024 to the Controller and Accountant General Department's payroll, with real-time validation and verification of employees' Ghana Card identities through biometric verification centres.
facts.system: NIA database integration with the Mechanized Payroll System

GHA.note: No civil register link is stated.

facts.fact: The National Identification Authority says the Mechanized Payroll System is operated by the Controller and Accountant General Department and was linked to the NIA database, launched 10 January 2024 by the Vice President, to validate public sector employees and pensioners.

GHA.note: The link is an integration with an existing payroll system, not stated as a replacement or upgrade of it.
No enrolment count or share is stated.
No number at birth is stated.
Who operates, maintains or owns the ID system is not stated.

facts.fact: The National Identification Authority says the civil service payroll (the Mechanized Payroll System) now requires the Ghana Card PIN to validate recruited public sector employees and pensioners, with existing staff to submit their PIN at NIA offices, launched 10 January 2024.
The National Identification Authority says the Ghana Card uniquely identifies its bearer on biographic and biometric features, held in a secure biometric national identification register.

GHA.note: Biometric check against double enrolment and security certification are not stated.

facts.fact: The National Identification Authority says the Controller and Accountant General Department's Mechanized Payroll System checks employees and pensioners against the NIA database by Ghana Card PIN, launched 10 January 2024, to remove ghost names.
facts.system: NIA database integration with the Mechanized Payroll System
